topStories.headline: A Pastrami Dream Heads to Irving Street: Mayer's Deli Eyes Early 2027 Opening
topStories.dek: A new Jewish delicatessen modeled on New York's legendary Katz's is set to open on Irving Street, joining a wave of new restaurants that has already transformed a five-block stretch of the Inner Sunset.
topStories.body:
Owner Josh Galant announced this week that Mayer's Delicatessen will open at 641 Irving St. in early 2027, taking over a space that has sat empty since the café Tart to Tart closed in 2022. Construction is nearly finished, Galant said, and neighbors have already noticed the deli's name spelled out in the tilework on the building's entryway floor. Pastrami will anchor the menu, using the same fatty cut of beef favored by New York Jewish deli institutions.

The announcement drops onto a strip of Irving Street that has absorbed more restaurant arrivals in 2026 than at any point in recent memory. Within a few blocks of the future Mayer's, world-renowned Neapolitan pizza chef Vincenzo Capuano opened his first U.S. restaurant at 822 Irving St. in late October; Oakland pizza favorite Mama's Boy is also planning an Inner Sunset location; and 403 Coffee, a Yemeni café, is in the works nearby.

Galant said Mayer's is opening on a strip that is 'really coming up when it comes to the food scene.' Some of the new arrivals have received help from SF New Deal's Neighborhood Vibrancy Fund, a nonprofit program that has backed up to 20 businesses with storefront and opening costs in the Inner Sunset. Mayer's was not among the grantees, but 403 Coffee and Mama's Boy both were.

The flurry of openings tracks with city sales-tax data showing the Inner Sunset has surpassed pre-pandemic revenue levels. Commercial strips further west — Taraval Street and Noriega Street in the Outer Sunset and Parkside — have not recovered to the same degree, and merchants there have described conditions as merely holding steady, with ongoing L-Taraval light-rail construction adding pressure on some blocks.

topStories.headline: World Pizza Champion Vincenzo Capuano Is Open on Irving Street — and More Are Coming
topStories.dek: The Neapolitan pizza chef who won the global Caputo Trophy opened his first U.S. restaurant in the Inner Sunset last month, and a new wave of arrivals is turning a stretch of Irving Street into one of the city's most watched food corridors.
topStories.body:
Vincenzo Capuano, who claimed the world championship of contemporary pizza at the Caputo Trophy in 2022 and operates more than two dozen restaurants across Europe and Asia, made his United States debut at 822 Irving St. in late October. The restaurant, Vincenzo Capuano SF, is a partnership between Capuano and Italian chef Osilio Florese, who also owns Mona Lisa Ristorante and Steps of Rome in North Beach. Its official opening day was October 23, preceded by a neighborhood party the week before.

The space had been occupied by Inle Burmese Cuisine, which closed in October after co-owner Morgan Sue cited health issues. Inle had relocated to the Inner Sunset from Noe Valley in 2023, and its departure after just three years on Irving Street left the space available almost immediately.

Capuano's arrival sits alongside several other announcements on the same corridor. The forthcoming Mayer's Delicatessen at 641 Irving St. and the planned Mama's Boy pizza outpost join 403 Coffee as businesses either open or under construction within a few blocks of one another. Tiles bearing Mayer's name appeared in the doorway of its future home this fall — a visual signal to the neighborhood that the momentum is real.

Food writers and merchants have begun comparing the five-block stretch to North Beach, long regarded as the city's premier dining district. Whether that energy spreads west to Taraval or Noriega remains to be seen; Outer Sunset and Parkside commercial corridors have continued to trail the Inner Sunset in sales-tax recovery, according to city data.

topStories.headline: Holiday Season Opens in the Inner Sunset with a Stroll, a Mercantile, and a Packed Shopping Street
topStories.dek: Irving Street is heading into its busiest holiday season in years, anchored by a December 5 evening stroll, a two-day mercantile in Golden Gate Park, and a retail mix that has grown considerably in 2026.
topStories.body:
The Inner Sunset is leaning into the holiday season with more commercial depth than it has had in several years. Local shops including Sunset Mercantile Emporium, Therapy Stores, and San Franpsycho are stocked with apparel, accessories, home décor, toys, and gifts. Vintage and secondhand options are available at Try Studio, Tight Knit Vintage & Modern, and Crossroads Trading, while children's boutiques Chloe's Closet and NOOMOON round out the mix on and near Irving Street.

The neighborhood's first major holiday event is the Inner Sunset Holiday Stroll on Saturday, December 5, running from 5 to 9 p.m. along Irving Street at Ninth Avenue. The same weekend, the 11th annual Sunset Holiday Mercantile takes over the County Fair Building in Golden Gate Park on December 5 and 6, with more than 100 local makers, food trucks, and live music acts and free admission for both days.

The Outer Sunset Farmers Market also returns on Sunday, December 6, offering fresh produce and artisan goods for shoppers on the western end of the district. And on December 11, the final Sunset Night Market of 2026 fills Irving Street between 20th and 25th avenues from 5 to 10 p.m., presented by People of Parkside Sunset. Taken together, the first two weekends of December shape up as the most event-dense holiday stretch these neighborhoods have seen all year.

moreNews.headline: Alan Wong Wins Full Four-Year Term as District 4 Supervisor
moreNews.body: Supervisor Alan Wong was re-elected to a full four-year term representing District 4 in the November 3 general election, defeating challengers Jeremy Greco and Albert Chow, according to the San Francisco Department of Elections. District 4 covers the Outer Sunset, Parkside, and Lakeshore neighborhoods west of 19th Avenue and has approximately 50,000 registered voters. Wong had previously won a special election earlier in 2026 to fill the remainder of former Supervisor Joel Engardio's term.

moreNews.headline: Parkside Filmmaker's 'Caring for Mom' Streams Free Through November 22
moreNews.body: A short documentary called 'Caring for Mom,' directed by Parkside resident and award-winning filmmaker Emeline Mann Sanchez, is available to stream free through November 22 as part of the online Legacy Film Festival on Aging. The film follows an elderly woman living with Alzheimer's and her caregiver, and encourages those in caregiving roles to find joy and adventure in the work.
